function: A raised watch over a landing and the road behind it. It sees, it holds a few fighters, and it gives whoever holds it somewhere to bring people in through -- reach, not manufacture.
height_class: [needs decision: height class for building.coast_watch_post -- brief section 20, exact standard building dimensions]

tier_states.notes: Walled, roofed, and worth garrisoning. The requirement flag is an Open placeholder; S13 owns what satisfies it.

dungeon_relationship: Provisional: too small to be a dungeon. A ruined post is a single space at most. S9 owns the signature.
loot_relationship: Provisional: whatever a garrison had on it. S10 owns loot tables.

notes: This record is the legal half of brief section 5.6's rule, authored on purpose so the refusal has something to be measured against. production.coast_watch_post.garrison_posting names a human_role, and it loads only because three things are true at once: the record does not list michael, interval_hours is 0 (a standing posting, never a timer that manufactures a person), and recruitment_support is non-empty and says what the support is. Change any one of the three and BuildingDefinition::validate and the buildings block in tools/src/validate.mjs both refuse it.
Open (brief section 20, exact resource list): construction_cost and every output_key carry the placeholder resource.open.needs_decision. No resource category is invented.

Open: the role key, the service key and both recruitment_support keys are *.open.needs_decision.* placeholders. There is no authored role, service or recruitment-support vocabulary yet, and inventing one here would decide a system this card does not own.

Open (brief section 20, exact standard building dimensions): height_class is a needs-decision placeholder; maximum_slope is 0 because the graph carries no slope; the envelope is a share of CELL_CAPACITY_CELLS, not metres.
Open (brief section 20, capture versus destruction rules by building type): chosen here -- a post is taken rather than levelled, and a knocked-down post leaves its platform footings on the ground.
Only two tiers are authored, below TIER_CAP. A record may author fewer tiers than the cap allows; the top production rule sits at minimum_tier 2, which is this record's top tier.
